recipes.title: Aglio e Olio with Greens & Chickpeas
recipes.eats: pasta (fusilli/penne), broccoli, canned chickpeas

summary.steps: boil pasta + broccoli (save a mug of water) → sizzle garlic & chilli in olive oil, warm chickpeas → toss in pasta, broccoli & a splash of water to emulsify → salt, pepper, lemon

recipes.blurb: The Roman classic, made a full meal: garlic, oil, chilli and lemon whipped with starchy pasta water into a glossy sauce, with chickpeas and broccoli carrying the protein, fibre and bite. Taste-led, and the payoff is well above the effort.
ingredients: 1 small head broccoli, cut into small florets
A generous glug extra-virgin olive oil (3–4 tbsp)
method: Boil the pasta in well-salted water. Drop the broccoli florets into the same pot for the last 3–4 minutes. Before draining, scoop out a mug of the starchy water.

Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a cold pan with the garlic and chilli over low–medium heat. Let them sizzle gently to pale gold and fragrant — don't let the garlic brown. Add the chickpeas and warm through, pressing a few against the pan so they catch a little.

Tip the drained pasta and broccoli into the pan with a good splash of pasta water. Toss hard for a minute so the oil and water emulsify into a glossy sauce that clings — add more pasta water if it looks oily.
Off the heat, season with salt and plenty of black pepper, then squeeze over the lemon and toss once more.
levelUp: **Cheesy & sharp (+ parmesan, not in kit):** a handful grated in off the heat tightens the emulsion and adds savoury depth.
**Crunch (+ toasted breadcrumbs or chopped almonds, not in kit):** toast dry in the pan first, scatter over at the end for contrast against the soft pasta.
**Fresh lift (+ flat-leaf parsley, not in kit):** a chopped handful stirred through brightens the whole bowl.
**Umami bomb (+ anchovy, not in kit):** melt one fillet into the garlic oil until it dissolves — it seasons everything; or swap the chickpeas for a tin of tuna (not in kit).
recipes.why: Taste is the point and it delivers — the garlic-chilli-lemon emulsion is genuinely excellent, and chickpeas plus broccoli turn it into a complete, nutrient-dense meal (plant protein, fibre, healthy fat). One continuous session, pot/pan/knife only, every ingredient on a normal shelf. The half-point on effort is just the careful garlic step and the toss to emulsify.

recipes.title: Apple-Cinnamon & Toasted Almond Oats
recipes.equipment: one pot / knife (a box grater helps but isn't essential)
recipes.eats: rolled oats, apple, almonds, Greek yoghurt

summary.steps: toast the almonds dry in the pot, tip out → grate in the apple with oats, water, cinnamon, ginger & a pinch of salt, simmer creamy → top with cool Greek yoghurt and the almonds

recipes.blurb: Apple-pie porridge: a whole apple grated straight into the oats half-melts into sweetness, warm cinnamon and a little ginger do the work of a spice rack, and cool Greek yoghurt plus dry-toasted almonds finish it with tang and crunch. The showcase for apple and almonds — taste-led, with no added sugar needed.
ingredients: A small handful (~25g) almonds, roughly chopped
1 apple, coarsely grated (skin on; core left behind)
A pinch of fine sea salt
method: Put the pot on medium heat and toast the chopped almonds dry, tossing, 3–4 min until golden and fragrant. Tip them out onto a plate.
Into the same pot add the oats, water, cinnamon, ginger and salt. Grate the apple straight in (stop at the core) and stir.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook, stirring now and then, 6–8 min until creamy and the apple has half-melted into the oats. Add a splash more water if it tightens too far.
Spoon into a bowl, top with a cool dollop of Greek yoghurt, and scatter over the toasted almonds. Eat hot.
levelUp: **Jammy sweetness (+ raisins or sultanas, not in kit):** stir a small handful in with the oats — they plump as they cook and melt into pockets of caramel sweetness.
**Drizzle to finish (+ tahini or honey, not in kit):** a thread of tahini over the yoghurt adds nutty richness, or honey if you want it properly dessert-like.
**Browner, nuttier almonds (+ butter, not in kit):** toast the almonds in a small knob of butter instead of dry for a brown-butter note that lifts the whole bowl.
**Omega-3 boost (+ ground flaxseed, not in kit):** stir a teaspoon into the finished oats for extra fibre and healthy fats without changing the flavour.
recipes.why: Taste leads — grated apple gives natural sweetness while cinnamon and ginger carry warmth, and the yoghurt-and-almond finish adds contrast in tang and crunch. Nutrition holds up: oat fibre, almond fats and Greek-yoghurt protein make it a balanced breakfast, not just carbs. And it's one pot, one continuous session, ~15 minutes start to bowl.

veganVariant.note: One ingredient swap — the Greek yoghurt finish — makes this fully vegan; everything else is already plant-based.
swaps: replace the 2–3 tbsp Greek yoghurt with plain plant yoghurt (oat or soy gives the closest tang)

recipes.title: Banana–Peanut Butter Oats
recipes.eats: rolled oats, banana, peanut butter, pumpkin seeds

summary.steps: simmer oats in water with a pinch of salt → mash in half a banana, cook to creamy → swirl in peanut butter and cinnamon off the heat → top with the rest of the banana, sliced, and pumpkin seeds

recipes.blurb: The default sweet bowl: oats simmered in water with half a mashed banana melting in for sweetness, a swirl of peanut butter for richness and staying power. No added sugar, no milk, no fridge — yet banana-and-PB is near-universally loved, so it earns its place on taste with effort close behind.
ingredients: 1 banana (½ mashed into the pot, ½ sliced for the top)
A small pinch of fine sea salt
method: Tip the oats, water and salt into the pot and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Mash half the banana and stir it in. Cook 4–5 min, stirring now and then, until thick and creamy and the oats are tender — add a splash more water if it tightens too much.
Off the heat, swirl through the peanut butter and cinnamon, leaving a few ribbons of PB visible.
Scrape into a bowl, fan the sliced banana over the top and scatter with pumpkin seeds. Eat hot.
levelUp: **Omega-3 & body (+ ground flaxseed or chia, not in kit):** stir a tablespoon in with the oats for a thicker bowl and a hit of omega-3 fat.
**Creamier cook (+ fortified plant milk, not in kit):** swap half the water for fortified plant milk for a richer porridge and added B12 and calcium.
**If the banana's underripe (+ honey or maple, not in kit):** a small drizzle rounds out the sweetness when the fruit alone doesn't carry it.
**PB–chocolate bowl (+ cocoa powder or dark chocolate, not in kit):** beat in a teaspoon of cocoa, or grate over a little dark chocolate, for a peanut-butter-cup finish.
recipes.why: Taste leads — banana and peanut butter is a crowd-pleaser, and cinnamon plus a pinch of salt keep it from cloying. Effort is right behind: one pot, one continuous session, ~10 minutes, nothing from the fridge and every item supermarket-anywhere. Nutrition holds its own too — whole oats and pumpkin seeds bring fibre and minerals, the peanut butter healthy fat and staying power, and the sweetness is all fruit, no added sugar.

recipes.title: Big Hummus & Avocado Wrap with Lemon Slaw
recipes.eats: wholemeal wrap, hummus, avocado, cabbage, carrot, pumpkin seeds

summary.steps: shred cabbage and carrot and toss with vinegar, salt and chilli → smash avocado with lemon and salt → spread hummus edge to edge on the wrap → pile on avocado, slaw and pumpkin seeds → roll tight and wrap in foil

recipes.blurb: The one truly portable, eat-anywhere dish: no heat at all, just creamy hummus and lemony avocado against a crunchy, tangy slaw, rolled tight and wrapped in foil to go.
ingredients: A big handful cabbage, finely shredded
½ carrot, grated or cut into thin matchsticks
method: Toss the shredded cabbage and carrot with the red wine vinegar, a good pinch of salt and the chilli flakes. Leave it to sit and soften while you do the rest.
Smash the avocado on a plate with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt — keep it a bit chunky.
Spread the hummus edge to edge across the wrap, right to the rim, so every bite has some.
Smear the avocado down the middle, pile on the slaw (lift it out of its liquid so the wrap stays dry), and scatter over the pumpkin seeds.
Fold in the sides, roll up tight from the bottom, and cut in half — or wrap it in foil and take it with you.
levelUp: **Protein lift (+ feta, not in kit; or a sliced boiled egg):** crumble feta or fold in a sliced egg for a real protein bump and extra body.
**Heat (+ pickled jalapeños or sriracha, not in kit):** a few slices or a squeeze of hot sauce for a sharp kick against the creamy fillings.
**Warm & substantial (+ halloumi, not in kit):** grate and pan-sear a slab, then layer it in hot for a heartier, melty wrap.
**Sturdier carry (+ corn tortilla or flatbread, not in kit):** swap to a thicker flatbread or double up if you're packing it for later.
recipes.why: Dominant criterion is **low effort** — zero cooking, no stove, just a knife and a few minutes of assembly, then it travels in foil with no further attention (effort 🟢). Hummus, avocado and pumpkin seeds stack fibre and healthy fats with cabbage and carrot for vitamin C, K and beta-carotene on a wholemeal base; protein is moderate, which the egg or feta lever fixes (nutrition 🟢). Every item is a supermarket staple (availability 🟢), and the creamy-against-crunchy, lemony-tangy contrast makes it genuinely good as-is (taste 🟢).

recipes.title: Black-Pepper Mushroom & Pak Choi with Egg
recipes.eats: mushroom, pak choi, eggs

summary.steps: hard-brown mushrooms in oil, season hard with black pepper → add garlic and pak choi (stems then leaves) with a splash of water, wilt, hit with red wine vinegar → fry the eggs crisp-edged and runny → slide over the veg, break the yolk as the sauce, finish with pepper and vinegar

recipes.blurb: Hard-browned mushrooms and wilted pak choi under a fried egg, heavy on cracked black pepper — deep, meaty umami without a drop of soy, the runny yolk doing the work of a sauce. It earns its place on taste: a stir-fry that eats far richer than its all-cupboard parts.
ingredients: A few big handfuls mushrooms, sliced thick
2 heads pak choi, stems and leaves separated, stems sliced
Plenty of black pepper, coarsely ground
A splash of red wine vinegar
method: Heat a good glug of rapeseed oil in the pan over high heat. Add the mushrooms and leave them largely undisturbed to release their water, then brown deeply, ~6–8 min — the colour is the flavour. Season with salt and a heavy grind of black pepper.

Add the garlic and the pak choi stems with a splash of water; toss 1–2 min until the stems are crisp-tender. Add the leaves and wilt ~1 min more. Splash in the red wine vinegar, toss once, then tip everything onto a plate.
Wipe the pan, add a little more oil, and fry the eggs over medium-high until the edges are crisp and lacy but the yolks still run. Crack lots of black pepper over them.
Slide the eggs onto the mushrooms and pak choi. Break the yolk so it sauces the vegetables; finish with salt, more pepper and a few drops of vinegar.
levelUp: **Glossy sauce (+ soy or oyster sauce + cornflour, both not in kit):** stir a teaspoon of cornflour into a splash of water with the soy or oyster sauce, then pour it in with the pak choi to coat everything in a clinging, takeaway-style gloss — and the soy deepens the umami the core builds without it.
**Aromatic base (+ ginger + spring onion, not in kit):** grate a thumb of ginger in with the garlic, and scatter sliced spring onion over at the end for freshness and lift.
**Toasty finish (+ sesame oil, not in kit):** a few drops swirled in off the heat for a nutty, sesame aroma.
**Make it heartier (+ firm tofu or butter, not in kit):** brown cubes of firm tofu alongside the mushrooms for extra protein, or melt a knob of butter into the pan with the eggs for richness.
recipes.why: Dominant criterion is **taste** — hard-browning the mushrooms and a fistful of black pepper build deep, meaty umami with no soy in sight, and the runny yolk turns it into a sauce. It's genuinely nutrient-dense too (complete protein, choline and B12 from the eggs; fibre, B-vitamins and selenium from the mushrooms; vitamin C, K, folate and calcium from the pak choi; healthy fat from the oil → nutrition 🟢). Every core item is an ordinary supermarket staple (availability 🟢), and it's one pan, one continuous session, ~10 minutes hands-on (effort 🟢).

recipes.title: Carrot, Cumin & Chickpea Pottage
recipes.eats: carrot, canned chickpeas

summary.steps: soften onion in oil → toast garlic, cumin, chilli → add carrot, chickpeas and water, simmer soft → mash velvety against the pot → finish with lemon, olive oil, black pepper

recipes.blurb: A tomato-free, naturally sweet bowl: carrots and chickpeas simmered soft, then hand-mashed to a velvety pottage — no blender, no fuss. Comfort food that happens to be a fibre-and-protein hit.
method: Warm a good glug of olive oil in the pot; soften the onion over medium heat, ~6 min, until sweet and translucent.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and chilli flakes; toast ~1 min until fragrant.

Add the carrots and chickpeas, a good pinch of salt, and just enough water to cover (~250ml). Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook ~20–25 min until the carrots are fork-soft. Scoop out a spoonful of whole chickpeas first if you want some texture to scatter back later.
Take off the heat and mash roughly against the side of the pot with a fork or the back of a spoon — velvety but not smooth, a few lumps welcome. Loosen with a splash of water if it's stiff.
Squeeze in the lemon, stir through a final drizzle of olive oil, and season hard with salt and black pepper. Top with the reserved chickpeas and an extra pinch of chilli.
levelUp: **Creamy and rich (+ coconut milk, not in kit):** stir a splash in at the mash stage for a silkier, fuller bowl — it tames the chilli and plays beautifully with the cumin.
**Warmer, deeper (+ fresh ginger, not in kit):** grate a thumb in with the garlic; (+ curry powder or harissa, not in kit) alongside the cumin pushes it toward a spiced dhal-soup.
**Cool tang on top (+ Greek yoghurt, not in kit):** a spoonful swirled in adds protein and a creamy contrast to the sweet carrot.
**Crunch and freshness (+ toasted pumpkin seeds and fresh coriander, not in kit):** seeds toasted in the dry pot before you start, scattered on with torn coriander, for healthy fat and lift.
recipes.why: Nutrition leads — chickpeas bring plant protein, iron and fibre, carrots load it with beta-carotene and more fibre, olive oil the healthy fat, and there's not a drop of anything empty in it. One pot, one continuous session, every item an ordinary shelf staple; the simmer time keeps effort at 🟡, but cumin, garlic, chilli and a hard squeeze of lemon make a comforting bowl that's genuinely worth eating.

recipes.title: Charred Broccoli & Crispy Cumin Chickpeas
recipes.eats: broccoli, canned chickpeas

summary.steps: dry-fry chickpeas nutty and crisp → char broccoli hard in oil → toss in garlic, cumin, chilli → return chickpeas, hard squeeze of lemon, salt, pepper

recipes.blurb: The vegan brassica powerhouse of the set: chickpeas dry-fried until crisp, broccoli charred to deep brown, pulled together with garlic, cumin and a hard hit of lemon. Eats just as well cold the next day.
ingredients: 1 can chickpeas, drained and patted dry
1 head broccoli, cut into small florets (slice any thick stem thin)
method: Heat the pan dry over medium-high; add the chickpeas and dry-fry, shaking now and then, until nutty and crisp, ~8 min. Salt, then tip onto a plate.

Add a good glug of olive oil and the broccoli, cut-side down. Leave it largely undisturbed to char hard, ~5–6 min; a splash of water and a brief cover helps the stems soften, then let it cook dry and colour.
Drop the heat, push the broccoli aside, and add the garlic, cumin and chilli flakes; toss ~1 min until fragrant.
Return the chickpeas, toss to combine, and take off the heat. Squeeze over the lemon, season with salt and plenty of black pepper.
levelUp: **Tahini-lemon drizzle (+ tahini, not in kit):** loosen tahini with lemon juice and a little water to a pourable sauce; spoon over for a creamy, nutty finish.
**Salty-cool contrast (+ feta, not in kit):** crumble feta over the warm pan so it half-melts against the charred edges.
**More crunch (+ flaked almonds or pumpkin seeds, not in kit):** toast in the dry pan before the chickpeas and scatter on at the end for extra healthy fat.
**Sticky-spicy glaze (+ honey and soy sauce, not in kit):** off the heat, add a drizzle of honey and a splash of soy sauce; toss so it clings to the chickpeas as a chilli-sweet glaze.
recipes.why: Nutrition leads — broccoli brings vitamin C, K, folate and fibre, chickpeas add plant protein and iron, olive oil the healthy fat. One pan, one session; every core item is an ordinary supermarket staple; and char plus cumin plus lemon makes it genuinely tasty hot or cold.

recipes.title: Charred Cabbage & Egg Pan
recipes.eats: cabbage, eggs

summary.steps: beat + salt eggs → scramble in hot oil until just set, lift out → char shredded cabbage hard in oil until the edges blacken and go sweet → add garlic + chilli → splash vinegar to deglaze, fold the eggs back through, season

recipes.blurb: Hard-charred cabbage turns sweet and nutty against soft scrambled egg, with garlic and chilli running through it. The cheapest veg on the shelf, on the plate in about a quarter of an hour — it earns its place on taste and how little it asks of you.
ingredients: ¼ cabbage, cut into rough 2 cm ribbons (a few big handfuls)
A splash of red wine vinegar
Rapeseed oil, fine sea salt, black pepper
method: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and a grind of pepper.
Heat a glug of oil in the pan over high heat. Pour in the eggs and scramble in big soft folds until just set, ~1 min. Lift them out while still glossy.

Add a little more oil, then the cabbage in as flat a layer as you can. Leave it undisturbed to catch and char, then toss and leave again, repeating until the edges blacken and the cabbage tastes sweet — 8–10 min.
Add the garlic and chilli and toss for ~30s until fragrant.
Splash in the red wine vinegar to deglaze and lift the char off the pan, then fold the eggs back through to warm. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper.
levelUp: **Egg-fried-rice depth (+ soy sauce, + sesame oil, both not in kit):** a splash of soy with the vinegar and a few drops of sesame oil off the heat give it savoury, toasty backbone.
**Aromatic lift (+ spring onion, + ginger, both not in kit):** grate in a little ginger with the garlic and scatter sliced spring onion over at the end.
**Make it a meal (+ cooked rice, not in kit):** fold a couple of handfuls of cold cooked rice in after the cabbage chars to turn it into a proper egg fried rice.
**More protein (+ edamame or firm tofu, not in kit):** toss frozen edamame or cubed tofu in with the cabbage for extra protein and bite.
recipes.why: Dominant criterion is **taste + effort** — hard charring is the one trick that makes cheap cabbage genuinely crave-able, and it all happens in one pan in a single unbroken session (effort 🟢). Eggs bring complete protein, choline and B12 alongside cabbage's fibre and vitamin C/K; nutrition is 🟡 only for being light on protein and grain-free, which the edamame/tofu and rice levers fix. Cabbage, eggs and garlic are everywhere (availability 🟢).

veganVariant.note: Crumbled firm tofu replaces the eggs, keeping the lift-out-and-fold-back structure; the result is golden and protein-rich rather than glossy-soft.
swaps: Replace the 3 eggs with 200g firm tofu, drained and crumbled into large chunks — cook in hot oil, stirring, until the edges turn golden (~3 min), then lift out and proceed exactly as written
Season the tofu with a pinch of turmeric alongside the salt for colour

recipes.title: Chickpea & Egg Deli Salad
recipes.eats: canned chickpeas, eggs, tomato

summary.steps: boil the eggs ~9 min while you work → quick-pickle sliced onion in vinegar and salt → chop tomato, drain chickpeas → peel and chop the eggs → fold everything with oil, lemon, chilli, salt and pepper

recipes.blurb: A room-temperature deli salad with double protein: creamy egg and chickpeas brightened by tomato and vinegar-quick-pickled onion. The only heat you need is a pot of boiling water, so it goes anywhere.
ingredients: 1 tomato, chopped (or a handful of tinned / cherry tomatoes)
Extra-virgin olive oil, fine sea salt, black pepper
method: Lower the eggs into a pot of boiling water and simmer 9 min for just-set yolks. Lift out and run under cold water until cool enough to peel.
While they cook, toss the sliced onion with the vinegar and a pinch of salt in your serving bowl — leave it to soften and turn pink.
Chop the tomato and tip in with the drained chickpeas. Add a good glug of olive oil, a squeeze of lemon, the chilli flakes, salt and plenty of black pepper.
Peel and roughly chop the eggs, fold them through gently, and check the seasoning. Eat warm or at room temp.
levelUp: **Salty protein boost (+ feta or tinned tuna, not in kit):** crumble feta or flake a drained tin of tuna through for brine, creaminess and even more protein.
**Deli freshness (+ fresh parsley or dill, not in kit):** a good handful chopped in lifts it to a proper deli-counter salad.
**Sharper dressing (+ wholegrain mustard, not in kit):** whisk a teaspoon into the oil and vinegar before folding for a tangy, clinging dressing.
**Creamy body (+ avocado, not in kit):** cube and fold in at the end for buttery richness and healthy fat.
recipes.why: Dominant criterion is **availability** — a tin of chickpeas, a few eggs and one onion are everywhere, and a single pot of boiling water is the only equipment. Chickpeas plus eggs stack plant and complete protein with fibre, B12, choline and iron (nutrition 🟢); it's one continuous session with no real cooking (effort 🟢). Core taste is good but plain — the deli-salad sparkle lives in the level-ups (taste 🟡).

recipes.title: Crispy Smoked-Paprika Tofu with Garlicky Greens & Pumpkin Seeds
recipes.eats: firm tofu, kale, spinach, pumpkin seeds

summary.steps: press and cube the tofu → toast pumpkin seeds in a dry pan, set aside → shallow-fry the tofu in rapeseed oil, turning each face until golden and crisp → off the heat, toss with smoked paprika, garlic granules and salt so the spice clings → in the same pan wilt garlicky, chilli-flecked kale then spinach with a squeeze of lemon → pile the tofu on the greens, shower with pumpkin seeds and more lemon

recipes.blurb: Pressed tofu cubed and shallow-fried until every face genuinely crackles — no coating, just the tofu's own crust — then tossed off the heat in smoked paprika and garlic granules so the spice clings, all piled on garlicky chilli greens and showered with toasted pumpkin seeds. The flagship crispy pan-fried tofu: it proves the texture is achievable kit-only, smoky-crisp protein against bright greens with no starch in sight.
ingredients: Fine sea salt and black pepper
method: Drain the tofu, wrap it in a clean tea towel or kitchen paper, sit a plate with a weight (a tin or full pan) on top, and press 15–20 min while you prep the rest. Cut into 2cm cubes and pat dry.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in the dry pan over medium heat, tossing, until they pop and colour, ~3 min. Tip out, season with a pinch of salt.

Add a generous layer of rapeseed oil and set over medium-high. Lay the tofu in one layer and — this is the whole trick — leave each face undisturbed until deep golden and crisp before turning, ~10 min for all sides. Lift onto kitchen paper.
Off the heat, tip the hot tofu into a bowl and toss with the smoked paprika, garlic granules, salt and black pepper so the spice clings to the crackly surface.

Pour most of the oil from the pan, add a splash of olive oil, the garlic and chilli flakes, and sizzle 20 sec. Add the kale with a splash of water; wilt 2 min. Add the spinach and wilt ~1 min more. Squeeze in lemon, season with salt.
Pile the greens onto a plate, heap the tofu on top, shower with pumpkin seeds and a final squeeze of lemon.
levelUp: **Sticky glaze (+ soy sauce + honey, not in kit):** off the heat, toss the crisp tofu in a splash of soy and a drizzle of honey instead of the dry spice for hot-honey, lacquered cubes.
**Max crunch (+ cornflour, not in kit):** dust the pressed cubes in a thin film of cornflour before frying for a shatter-crisp shell that stays crunchy longer.
**Nutty top (+ sesame seeds or tahini, not in kit):** scatter toasted sesame over the seeds, or loosen tahini with lemon and water into a drizzle over the greens.
**Make it a plate (+ rice or warm flatbread, not in kit):** serve over rice or with flatbread to mop up the garlicky, paprika-stained oil.
recipes.why: Dominant criterion is **nutrition** — two protein sources on one plate (firm tofu plus pumpkin seeds, which also bring magnesium, zinc and healthy fat), iron and calcium from the tofu, and a heavy load of vitamin K, C, folate and fibre from the kale and spinach, all carried in good oils with no starch padding it out (nutrition 🟢). Taste is strong too: crisp, smoky tofu against bright garlicky greens (taste 🟢). Every core item is an ordinary supermarket staple (availability 🟢). It's one pan and one session, but pressing the tofu and frying it patiently to a real crust make it the most hands-on of the one-pan dinners (effort 🟡).

recipes.title: Crunchy Cabbage & Carrot Slaw with Cumin Chickpeas
recipes.eats: cabbage, carrot, canned chickpeas

summary.steps: whisk a cumin–lemon–vinegar dressing in the bowl and steep the sliced onion in it → shred cabbage and grate carrot → fold in drained chickpeas and toss → eat now or let it sit and keep for days

recipes.blurb: A no-cook slaw you shred once and live off for days: cabbage and carrot stay crunchy, cumin and chilli warm the dressing, and chickpeas turn it into a real meal. It only gets better as it sits in the fridge.
ingredients: ¼ small cabbage, finely shredded (a few big handfuls)
1 large carrot, grated or cut into thin matchsticks
method: In your serving bowl, whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, vinegar, cumin, chilli flakes, a good pinch of salt and plenty of black pepper. Stir the sliced onion in and leave it to mellow while you do the rest.
Finely shred the cabbage and grate (or matchstick) the carrot — the thinner you go, the better they soften and drink up the dressing.
Tip the cabbage, carrot and drained chickpeas into the bowl and toss well so everything is coated. Taste and adjust salt and lemon.
Eat straight away, or leave it 15–30 min (or chill overnight) — it improves as the veg softens and the flavours meld. Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge.
levelUp: **Creamy coleslaw turn (+ Greek yoghurt, not in kit):** stir a couple of spoonfuls into the dressing for a tangy, creamy slaw and a protein bump.
**Satay lean (+ peanut butter, not in kit; + lime, not in kit):** whisk a spoon of peanut butter and a squeeze of lime into the dressing for a nutty, slaw-noodle-style hit.
**Crunch & good fat (+ toasted peanuts or sunflower seeds, not in kit):** scatter a handful over the top for texture and healthy fat.
**Fresh & sweet (+ fresh coriander, not in kit; + grated apple or sultanas, not in kit):** a handful of chopped coriander and some grated apple or a few sultanas lift and round it out.
recipes.why: Dominant criterion is **low effort** — no stove, no cooking, one knife and one bowl, done in about 10 minutes and then it feeds you for days with zero further attention (effort 🟢). Chickpeas bring protein and fibre, cabbage and carrot pile on vitamin C, K and beta-carotene, and the olive oil adds healthy fat (nutrition 🟢); every ingredient is a supermarket staple (availability 🟢). The core is a genuinely good everyday slaw — punchy with cumin, chilli and onion — but it's plain until a creamy or nutty dressing and some fresh herbs take it up a level (taste 🟡).

recipes.title: Cumin Pepper, Carrot & Chickpea Stir-fry
recipes.eats: bell pepper, carrot, canned chickpeas

summary.steps: dry-fry chickpeas crisp → blister peppers and carrots hard in oil → add onion, garlic, cumin, chilli → return chickpeas, splash of vinegar, salt, pepper

recipes.blurb: A Xinjiang-leaning stir-fry: peppers and carrots blistered hard, crisp-edged chickpeas, and a heavy hand of cumin and chilli. Vegan, fast, and a real protein-and-fibre hit.
ingredients: 2 medium carrots, cut into thin matchsticks
1 can chickpeas, drained and patted dry
A good pinch of chilli flakes
method: Heat the pan dry over medium-high; add the chickpeas and dry-fry, shaking now and then, until nutty and crisp, ~7 min. Salt, then tip onto a plate.

Add a good glug of rapeseed oil and turn the heat high. Add the peppers and carrots and stir-fry hard, leaving them to sit between tosses so they blister and char, ~5 min. A splash of water and a brief cover softens the carrot if it needs it.
Add the onion, garlic, cumin and chilli flakes; toss ~2 min until fragrant and the onion just softens.
Return the chickpeas, splash in the vinegar and let it sizzle off, then season hard with salt and plenty of black pepper. Serve straight from the pan.
levelUp: **Umami depth (+ soy sauce, not in kit):** swap the vinegar splash for soy, or use both, for a savoury, restaurant-style finish.
**Fresh heat and lift (+ fresh chilli and ginger, not in kit):** a grated thumb of ginger and a sliced red chilli in with the garlic push it brighter and more aromatic.
**Herby, citrus finish (+ fresh coriander and lime, not in kit):** scatter torn coriander and squeeze lime over off the heat for a Xinjiang-night-market lift.
**Smoke and crunch (+ smoked paprika and peanuts, not in kit):** a teaspoon of paprika with the cumin, a handful of toasted peanuts on top for healthy fat and bite.
recipes.why: Nutrition leads — chickpeas bring plant protein, iron and fibre, peppers load it with vitamin C, carrots add beta-carotene, and rapeseed oil the healthy fat, with nothing empty in the pan. One pan, one continuous session, every item an ordinary supermarket staple; high-heat blistering plus a heavy hand of cumin, chilli and a vinegar hit make it genuinely tasty — effort sits at 🟡 only because the matchsticks and constant tossing want tending.

summary.steps: boil pasta in salted water → fry shredded cabbage and onion hard in olive oil until the edges frizzle → add garlic, cumin, chilli and chickpeas to crisp → toss with drained pasta, a splash of pasta water, lemon and salt

recipes.blurb: Cabbage fried hard until the edges go sweet, charred and nutty, with cumin-warmed chickpeas folded through pasta. Cheap, long-keeping veg that eats like much more than it cost.
ingredients: ¼ cabbage, shredded (a few big handfuls)
1 can chickpeas, drained and patted dry
Extra-virgin olive oil, fine sea salt
method: Boil the pasta in well-salted water. Scoop out a mugful of the water before draining.
Meanwhile, heat a generous glug of olive oil in the pan over high heat. Add the cabbage and onion and fry hard, stirring only now and then, until the edges char and frizzle — 8–10 min.
Push to one side; add the chickpeas, garlic, cumin and chilli and let the chickpeas crisp and the garlic soften, ~3 min. Salt to taste.
Toss in the drained pasta with a splash of the pasta water to loosen. Squeeze over the lemon, check the salt, and serve.
levelUp: **Salty creamy finish (+ feta, not in kit):** crumble over off the heat — its sharp tang cuts the sweet cabbage.
**Deeper char (+ smoked paprika, not in kit):** a teaspoon in with the cumin adds smoke that doubles down on the frizzle.
**Crunch (+ pumpkin or sunflower seeds, not in kit):** toast dry in the pan first and scatter on top for texture and extra healthy fat.
**Earthier swap (+ tinned green lentils, not in kit):** use in place of chickpeas for a softer, more savoury bite.
recipes.why: Dominant criterion is **availability** — cabbage, an onion, a tin of chickpeas and dry pasta are everywhere and keep for weeks. Chickpeas and cabbage carry real protein, fibre and vitamin C/K (nutrition 🟢); it's one pot, one pan, one session (effort 🟡 only because the hard frizzle wants tending). recipes.title: Frozen Pea & Egg, Lemon-Bright
recipes.eats: frozen peas, eggs

summary.steps: bloom a smashed garlic clove in oil → simmer frozen peas in a splash of water → fold in beaten eggs to a soft scramble → off heat: lemon, chilli, pepper, a final drizzle of oil

recipes.blurb: Sweet peas straight from the freezer, soft eggs and a hit of lemon — bright, satisfying, and not a single thing to chop. The whole dish leans on store-cupboard and freezer staples, so it's the one to make when you've got five spare minutes and zero patience.
ingredients: 3–4 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
1 clove garlic, smashed flat with the side of the knife (no chopping)
½ lemon (a little zest if you have it, plus the juice)
method: Warm a good glug of olive oil over medium heat; add the smashed garlic and let it perfume the oil ~1 min, then lift it out (or leave it — your call).
Tip in the frozen peas with a splash of water; cook, stirring now and then, until bright green and tender, ~3–4 min. Season lightly.
Drop the heat to low. Pour in the beaten eggs and stir gently, folding through the peas, until just softly set — ~1–2 min. Don't overcook; they finish off the heat.
Off the heat, squeeze over the lemon (and a little zest), scatter chilli flakes and plenty of black pepper, and finish with a thread of olive oil.
levelUp: **Salty crumble (+ feta or shaved parmesan, not in kit):** scatter over the warm eggs so it half-melts into them for a savoury anchor.
**Fresh lift (+ torn mint, not in kit):** mint and peas are a classic; tear a few leaves over at the end for a cool, sweet edge.
**Creamy spoon (+ Greek yoghurt or crème fraîche, not in kit):** a dollop alongside turns it richer and more breakfast-like, and tames the chilli.
**Make it a full plate (+ toast, or flaked hot-smoked salmon / sliced avocado, not in kit):** pile onto hot toast, or fold through flaked salmon or avocado for protein and staying power.
recipes.why: Effort leads — no board, no chopping, one pan, one continuous session, peas straight from the freezer. Nutrition keeps pace: complete protein and healthy fat from the eggs and oil, fibre, plant protein and vitamin C from the peas, micronutrients from the lemon. Every core item is an ordinary supermarket staple, and sweet peas against soft egg, bright lemon and a little heat make it genuinely good to eat.

recipes.title: Garlicky Mushrooms & Spinach with Runny Eggs
recipes.eats: mushroom, spinach, eggs

summary.steps: Sear sliced mushrooms hard until deep golden → add garlic, chilli & spinach to wilt → make wells, crack in eggs, cover till whites set and yolks runny → finish with salt, pepper, lemon

recipes.blurb: The kale-mushroom sauté grown up: hard-seared umami mushrooms and wilted spinach under runny yolks, now a complete egg-protein meal in one pan. Taste leads — everything else comes free.
method: Heat a good glug of olive oil in the pan over medium-high. Add the mushrooms in one layer and leave them undisturbed 3–4 min, then turn and sear the other side until deep golden and shrunken — don't crowd or rush them; the hard sear is the whole flavour. Season with salt.
Drop the heat a little. Add the garlic and chilli flakes; cook 30–60 sec until fragrant.
Pile in the spinach and stir until just wilted — a minute for fresh, a little longer for frozen (let the water cook off).

Spread the veg out and make 2–3 wells. Crack an egg into each, season the whites, and cover with a lid or plate (or spoon the hot oil over them) until the whites set but the yolks stay runny, 2–4 min.
Off the heat, squeeze over lemon and grind on black pepper. Eat straight from the pan.
levelUp: **Toast underneath (+ bread, not in kit):** pile everything onto a slice of toast so the runny yolk and garlicky oil soak in — turns it into a fuller meal.
**Deeper umami (+ soy sauce, not in kit):** splash a teaspoon over the mushrooms as they finish searing to amplify the savoury hit.
**Make it heartier (+ tinned cannellini or white beans, not in kit):** warm a drained handful with the mushrooms for extra protein and fibre.
**Savoury finish (+ grated parmesan, not in kit):** shower over at the end, or swirl in a knob of butter (not in kit) for a glossier, richer pan.
recipes.why: Taste is the dominant criterion and it delivers — a hard sear concentrates the mushrooms' umami and the runny yolk becomes a sauce, kept bright by chilli and lemon. Underneath that it's genuinely complete: egg protein, mushroom and spinach micronutrients, healthy fat from the oil — all in one pan, one continuous session, from nine everyday ingredients.

swaps: Replace the 2–3 eggs with a drained 400 g tin of chickpeas — add them with the garlic and chilli and crisp at the edges for 2–3 min
Stir in a teaspoon of nutritional yeast with the spinach for the savoury depth the yolk would have given

recipes.title: Golden Lentil & Turmeric Oats (Dal Porridge)
recipes.eats: red split lentils, rolled oats, spinach

summary.steps: temper onion, garlic, turmeric, cumin, ginger & chilli in oil → add rinsed lentils + water, simmer until collapsing → stir in oats, cook to a thick golden porridge → wilt spinach through, finish with lemon, salt & pepper

recipes.blurb: Savoury oats gone full khichdi: red split lentils simmered soft with turmeric, cumin and ginger, then oats stirred in to thicken everything into a golden porridge, spinach wilted through and lemon to finish. Lentil-plus-oat makes it a complete-protein, iron-rich one-pot bowl — the meat-free, egg-free flagship of the savoury breakfast side, and a clear step away from the cumin-peas-egg oats.
ingredients: A pinch of chilli flakes (plus more to finish)
method: Rinse the lentils in a sieve until the water runs clear; set aside. Warm the oil in the pot over medium and soften the onion 3–4 min, then add the garlic, turmeric, cumin, ground ginger and chilli flakes and fry ~1 min until fragrant and deep gold.
Tip in the lentils and the water. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring now and then so they don't catch, ~15 min, until the lentils swell and start to collapse into a loose dal.
Stir in the oats and simmer another 4–5 min, stirring, until thick and porridge-like. Loosen with a splash more water if it tightens past spoonable.

Fold the spinach through to wilt, ~1 min. Take off the heat, season hard with salt and black pepper, and squeeze in the lemon. Taste and push the cumin, chilli or lemon until it reads warm and bright. Serve hot with a final pinch of chilli.
levelUp: **More protein on top (+ egg, in kit):** crown the bowl with a jammy or fried egg — the runny yolk enriches the porridge and pushes it past 25 g protein.

**Real tadka (+ black mustard seeds, not in kit):** pop a teaspoon of mustard seeds in a little hot oil until they crackle, then pour the sizzling oil over each bowl — the defining finish of a proper dal.

**Brighter, fresher dal (+ fresh ginger, green chilli & coriander, not in kit):** grate in fresh ginger and a sliced green chilli with the aromatics, and scatter torn coriander at the end for a livelier, more fragrant bowl.
**Creamy finish (+ coconut milk, not in kit):** stir in a splash of coconut milk off the heat for a richer, rounder, gently sweet porridge.
recipes.why: Nutrition leads — red lentils and oats together make a complete protein with serious fibre and iron, turmeric and ginger bring anti-inflammatory warmth, spinach adds folate and more iron, and rapeseed oil the healthy fat, all in one pot with nothing empty. It's ordinary shelf staples over one unbroken session (availability 🟢), though the ~15-minute lentil simmer plus the constant-stir oat phase keep effort at 🟡. Toasted spices, garlic and a hard squeeze of lemon make the water-based core genuinely good; an egg or a real tadka takes it to great (taste 🟡).

recipes.title: Groundnut Peanut & Red Lentil Stew
recipes.eats: red split lentils, peanut butter, tinned chopped tomato, spinach, kale

summary.steps: soften onion & garlic in oil → bloom curry powder, paprika, cumin, ginger, chilli → add tomato, lentils & water and simmer till soft → stir in peanut butter till creamy → wilt greens through, season

recipes.blurb: A West-African-style one-pot: red lentils simmered into tomato and a warm curry-paprika-ginger base, then enriched with a heaped spoon of peanut butter that melts the whole thing creamy, with greens wilted through. Pantry spices alone carry it — the peanut-tomato richness does the heavy lifting.
ingredients: 2 big handfuls spinach and/or kale (kale stems removed), roughly chopped
method: Warm a glug of rapeseed oil in the pot over medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook 5–6 min until soft and golden at the edges.
Drop the heat, add the garlic, curry powder, paprika, cumin, ground ginger and chilli flakes, and stir ~1 min until the spices smell toasty — don't let them scorch.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and cook 2–3 min to a thick paste, then tip in the lentils and the water. Season with salt and bring to a simmer.
Simmer 20–25 min, stirring now and then so the lentils don't catch on the base, until they've collapsed into a soft, thick stew. Add a splash of water if it tightens too far.

Stir in the peanut butter until it melts through and the stew turns creamy and glossy. Fold in the greens and cook 2–3 min until wilted (kale a touch longer than spinach). Taste for salt, chilli and a little more peanut butter if you want it richer.
levelUp: **Savoury depth (+ stock cube or bouillon and tomato purée, not in kit):** crumble a stock cube into the water and fry a spoon of tomato purée with the spices for a rounder, more savoury base.
**Rounder and richer (+ coconut milk, not in kit):** stir a splash through at the end for a silkier, mellower stew that tames the chilli.
**Fresh lift (+ fresh ginger, chilli, lime and coriander, not in kit):** grate in fresh ginger and chilli with the garlic, then finish with a squeeze of lime and torn coriander to cut the richness.
**Make it a plate (+ rice and roasted peanuts, not in kit):** spoon over rice and scatter crushed roasted peanuts on top for crunch.
recipes.why: Nutrition leads — red lentils bring plant protein and fibre, peanut butter adds healthy fat and more protein, and the spinach and kale load it with micronutrients, all from tomato-rich one-pot comfort. Every item is an ordinary shelf staple and all-proven (availability 🟢), and the peanut-tomato base tastes far slower-cooked than it is (taste 🟢). It's one pot in one session, but lentils want ~25 min of occasional stirring so they don't catch, so effort is good rather than effortless (🟡).

summary.steps: boil eggs ~6½ min for jammy yolks → soak sliced onion in vinegar + salt → toss spinach + tomato with oil, lemon, chilli → halve eggs over the salad, break the yolk in as dressing

recipes.blurb: A raw tomato-and-spinach salad with halved jammy eggs on top: the only cooking is the pot of boiling water, and the soft runny yolk breaks down into the dressing as you eat. Built for taste on a genuinely nutritious base.

Extra-virgin olive oil, fine sea salt, black pepper
method: Lower the eggs into a pot of gently boiling water and simmer 6½ min for jammy yolks (set white, soft runny centre). Lift out and sit in cold water until cool enough to peel.
While they cook, toss the sliced onion with the vinegar and a pinch of salt in your serving bowl — leave it to soften and lose its raw bite.
Add the tomato and spinach. Dress with a good glug of olive oil, a squeeze of lemon, the chilli flakes, salt and black pepper, and toss to coat and slightly wilt the spinach.
Peel the eggs and halve them over the salad, cut-side up. Sprinkle the yolks with a little salt, pepper and chilli, then break into them as you eat so the yolk runs through as a rich dressing.

**Make it a plate (+ toast or croutons, not in kit):** serve over toast or scatter torn croutons in for crunch and to mop the yolk.

recipes.eats: canned chickpeas, eggs, spinach

summary.steps: boil eggs to jammy, cold-shock → fork-smash chickpeas with lemon, oil, chilli, salted onion → dress raw spinach, pile on the chickpeas, halve the eggs over the top, finish with oil, lemon, pepper

recipes.blurb: The lowest-effort way to get a hot protein on the plate: you boil an egg, and the rest is fork-and-assemble. Lemony smashed chickpeas and jammy yolks over raw spinach — fresh, honest, and done before the kettle's cooled.
method: Bring a small pot of water to the boil. Lower in the eggs and simmer 6½ minutes for a jammy yolk, then tip into cold water to stop them — peel when cool enough to handle.
While they cook, put the diced onion in a bowl with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon; leave it to mellow (the acid takes the raw bite off).
Add the chickpeas, a good glug of olive oil, the chilli flakes and more lemon. Fork-smash to a rough, craggy mash — some whole, some crushed. Season with salt and black pepper; taste for lemon.

Dress the spinach with a little oil, a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt, and spread it over a plate or bowl. Pile the smashed chickpeas on top, halve the peeled eggs and lay them over, and finish with a thread of oil, black pepper and a last pinch of chilli.
levelUp: **Creamy backbone (+ tahini, not in kit):** loosen a spoon of tahini with lemon and water and swirl it through the chickpeas — turns the rough mash silky and rich.
**Cool and tangy (+ Greek yoghurt, not in kit):** a dollop spooned underneath, or feta crumbled (+ feta, not in kit) over the top, adds protein and a salty-sour lift.
**Make it greener (+ fresh parsley or coriander, not in kit):** a fistful of chopped herbs through the chickpeas brings it alive; sliced cucumber (+ cucumber, not in kit) adds crunch.
**Carry it (+ pita or toast, not in kit):** scoop everything onto warm pita or toast to turn the bowl into a proper handheld meal.
recipes.why: Effort leads — a single pot, one unbroken session, and the only cooking is a boiled egg, so it's the easiest hot-protein dish in the set. Nutrition keeps up: chickpeas bring fibre, plant protein and iron, eggs add complete protein with choline and B12, spinach folate and vitamin K, olive oil the healthy fat. Every item is an ordinary supermarket staple. Taste is the honest trade — fresh and clean rather than rich, which is exactly what the tahini, yoghurt and feta levers are there to fix.

recipes.title: Mackerel & Oat Fishcakes, Smoky Paprika
recipes.eats: tinned mackerel, rolled oats, eggs, frozen peas

summary.steps: mash mackerel with beaten egg, onion, garlic granules, smoked paprika & oats → rest 5 min so the oats drink up the moisture → form patties → pan-fry both sides to a crisp golden crust → simmer peas in the same pan → plate with lemon

recipes.blurb: Fishcakes with no potato to boil and no oven — rolled oats are the binder, soaking up the oil and moisture before crisping to a savoury, golden crust. A no-waste way to make a tin feel like a proper cooked meal, and the mix keeps and fries in batches.
method: Tip the drained mackerel into a bowl and mash with a fork. Add the beaten egg, onion, garlic granules, paprika and oats, with a squeeze of lemon, salt and a good grind of pepper. Mix to an even, slightly sticky mash.
Let it sit 5 minutes — the oats swell and drink up the moisture, firming the mix so it holds. With damp hands, press into 4 patties about 1.5cm thick.
Heat a thin layer of oil in the pan over medium. Fry the patties, undisturbed, 3–4 min a side until deep golden and crisp — flip once, gently. Lift onto a plate.
Tip the frozen peas into the same pan with a splash of water, simmer 2–3 min until bright and hot, season, and lightly crush a few with the fork.
Spoon the peas alongside, set the fishcakes on top, and finish with the rest of the lemon squeezed over.
levelUp: **Sauce it (+ Greek yoghurt, in kit; + Dijon, not in kit):** whip Greek yoghurt with lemon and a little salt for a quick dip — or stir in Dijon for a tartare-ish tang.
**Fresh aromatics (+ spring onion + fresh coriander, not in kit):** fold sliced spring onion and chopped coriander through the mix for lift and colour.
**Sweet-sharp glaze (+ sweet chilli or sriracha, not in kit):** brush a little over the patties in the last minute so it catches and caramelises.
**Crunchier crust (+ panko breadcrumbs, not in kit):** press the formed patties into panko before frying for an extra-shattering coat.
recipes.why: Nutrition leads — oily mackerel brings omega-3, B12 and vitamin D, the egg and peas add complete protein and fibre, and the oat binder folds in beta-glucan instead of plain starch. It's one pan in a single session from ordinary shelf staples; the only ding is that forming and flipping patties is a touch more hands-on than a stir-together bowl, and the smoky-paprika crust with lemon makes it genuinely good to eat.

recipes.title: Pasta e Ceci (One-Pot Chickpea Pasta)
recipes.eats: pasta (fusilli/penne), canned chickpeas, tinned chopped tomato

summary.steps: soften onion, garlic & chilli in oil → cook down the tomato → add chickpeas and mash a third → pour in water, simmer → stir in the pasta and cook till tender and creamy → season

recipes.blurb: The pasta cooks right in a garlicky chickpea-tomato broth, with a third of the chickpeas mashed so the whole thing turns silky and creamy. One pot, nothing to drain, deeply savoury — pantry food that eats like a treat.
ingredients: 150g pasta (fusilli or penne — short shapes fit the pot)
Optional (still core): 2 handfuls spinach, stirred in at the end for a green
method: Warm a good glug of olive oil in the pot; soften the onion 4–5 min, then add the garlic and a pinch of chilli flakes for 1 min.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes; cook down 3–4 min to a thick, jammy paste.
Add the chickpeas and mash about a third of them against the side of the pot — this is what makes the broth creamy.
Pour in the water, season with salt, and bring to a steady simmer.

Stir in the pasta. Simmer 10–12 min, stirring often so it doesn't catch, until the pasta is tender and the broth has thickened around it. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens too far. Stir through the spinach to wilt, if using. Finish with black pepper and a drizzle of olive oil.
levelUp: **Cheese it (+ parmesan, not in kit):** grate parmesan over each bowl, and drop a rind into the broth at step 4 to simmer — deep, savoury umami for almost no effort.
**Herb backbone (+ fresh rosemary or a bay leaf, not in kit):** add a small sprig of rosemary or a bay leaf with the tomatoes; fish it out before serving for a warm, aromatic lift.
**More legume body (+ tinned cannellini or tinned lentils, not in kit):** swap or top up some of the chickpeas — cannellini melt creamier, lentils add an earthy bite.
**Silk finish (+ a splash of cream or yoghurt, not in kit):** stir a spoonful through off the heat for a rounder, richer broth.
recipes.why: Everything is ordinary-supermarket, all-proven stock (availability 🟢), and the mash-a-third trick turns a flat pantry into a genuinely creamy, savoury bowl (taste 🟢). Chickpeas carry plant protein and fibre, with tomato and olive oil rounding out the nutrition — better still with the optional spinach (🟢). It's one pot and one session with nothing to drain, but the pasta cooks in the broth and wants frequent stirring so it doesn't catch, so effort is good rather than effortless (🟡).

recipes.title: Peanut Tofu with Cabbage & Pak Choi
recipes.eats: firm tofu, peanut butter, cabbage, pak choi, carrot, pumpkin seeds

summary.steps: whisk a satay sauce from peanut butter, garlic, ginger, chilli, lemon and water → pan-fry tofu cubes crisp and golden, set aside → stir-fry carrot and cabbage hard, then pak choi → return tofu, pour over the sauce to glaze, finish with pumpkin seeds and lemon

recipes.blurb: A quick satay-style bowl: crisp pan-fried tofu and a fast cabbage-carrot-pak choi stir-fry turned glossy in a creamy, savoury, lemon-sharp peanut sauce. The sauce is the whole draw — and it proves peanut butter pulls its weight as a serious savoury main, not just a toast spread.
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu (~280g), patted very dry, cut into 2cm cubes
2 cloves garlic, crushed or finely grated
A good pinch of chilli flakes
Juice of ½ lemon (plus a wedge to finish)
2 heads pak choi, stems and leaves separated, stems sliced
method: Make the sauce: in a mug or small bowl, whisk the peanut butter, garlic, ground ginger, chilli flakes, lemon juice and a pinch of salt with warm water, a splash at a time, until smooth and pourable like single cream. Set aside.

Heat a good glug of rapeseed oil in the pan over medium-high. Add the tofu and fry, turning every couple of minutes, until deeply golden and crisp on several sides, ~8–10 min. Salt, then tip onto a plate.

Add a little more oil and turn the heat high. Add the carrot and cabbage and stir-fry hard, ~3–4 min, with a splash of water to steam them tender-crisp. Add the pak choi stems for a minute, then the leaves, and toss until just wilted.
Return the tofu, pour over the peanut sauce and toss to glaze everything (loosen with a splash of water if it tightens). Scatter pumpkin seeds over the top and serve with the lemon wedge.
levelUp: **Proper satay balance (+ soy sauce, + lime, + honey, not in kit):** a splash of soy for salt, lime in place of lemon, and a teaspoon of honey whisked into the sauce gives the full salty-sour-sweet trio that makes satay sing.
**Heat & aroma (+ sriracha, + sesame oil, not in kit):** a squeeze of sriracha into the sauce and a few drops of sesame oil swirled in off the heat for a nutty, fiery lift.
**Make it a noodle bowl (+ rice noodles, not in kit; or pasta, in kit):** toss cooked rice noodles or fusilli through at the end so the peanut sauce coats them — a fuller, more filling plate.
**Fresh top (+ coriander, spring onion, crushed peanuts, not in kit):** torn coriander, sliced spring onion and a few crushed peanuts scattered over for freshness and extra crunch.
recipes.why: Dominant criterion is **taste** — the creamy, savoury, lemon-sharp peanut sauce glazing crisp tofu and just-wilted greens eats far richer than its cupboard parts. It's also genuinely nutrient-dense: complete plant protein and calcium from the tofu, more protein and healthy fat from peanut butter and pumpkin seeds, and fibre plus vitamin C, K and beta-carotene from the cabbage, pak choi and carrot (nutrition 🟢). Every core item is an ordinary supermarket staple (availability 🟢); it's one pan and one continuous session, sitting at effort 🟡 only because crisping the tofu and shredding the veg want a bit of tending.

recipes.title: Red Lentil Ragù with Pasta (Lentil "Bolognese")
recipes.equipment: one pot, one pan (or second pot), knife
recipes.eats: red split lentils, pasta (fusilli/penne), carrot, tinned chopped tomato

summary.steps: soften onion & carrot in oil until jammy → add garlic, oregano & chilli → stir in tomato, lentils & water and simmer to a thick, glossy ragù → boil pasta separately → finish the sauce with vinegar, then toss the pasta through with a splash of its water

recipes.blurb: Red split lentils cooked down with a slow soffritto and tomato into a thick, glossy, almost-meaty sauce, tossed through fusilli — a lentil bolognese that hits the pasta core from a different angle than Pasta e Ceci. Oregano, jammy onion and a splash of vinegar give it real ragù depth, loaded with plant protein and fibre. Double the sauce; it freezes well.
ingredients: ~400 ml water, plus more if needed
Extra-virgin olive oil, fine sea salt, black pepper
method: Warm a generous glug of olive oil in the pot over medium heat. Add the onion and carrot with a pinch of salt and cook slowly, stirring now and then, until soft and jammy — 8–10 min. Stir in the garlic, oregano and chilli flakes and cook 1 min until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomatoes and rinsed lentils, pour in the water, and season with salt. Bring to a steady simmer.
Simmer 25–30 min, stirring occasionally so it doesn't catch and loosening with a splash of water if it tightens too far, until the lentils have collapsed into a thick, glossy ragù.
Meanwhile, boil the pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the water before draining.

Stir the red wine vinegar into the sauce and check the salt and pepper. Fold the drained pasta through, loosening with a splash of pasta water so it coats. Finish with black pepper and a drizzle of olive oil.
levelUp: **Cheese & gloss (+ parmesan and a knob of butter, not in kit):** grate parmesan over and stir butter through off the heat — richer, rounder, more classically bolognese.
**Deeper base (+ tomato purée, not in kit):** bloom a spoon of purée with the garlic and oregano for a minute before the tomatoes; it adds concentrated, savoury depth.
**Meaty backbone (+ soy sauce or Worcestershire, not in kit):** a splash in with the water brings umami and that long-cooked, almost-meaty edge.
**Extra body (mushrooms, in kit):** brown a handful of diced mushrooms in the oil before the onion for more texture and meatiness.
recipes.why: Everything is ordinary-supermarket, all-proven stock (availability 🟢), and lentils simmered with soffritto, tomato, oregano and a hit of vinegar make a genuinely glossy, savoury ragù (taste 🟢). Red lentils bring big plant protein and fibre, with carrot, tomato and olive oil rounding out the nutrition (🟢). recipes.title: Sardine, Avocado & Lemon Smash on Seeded Toast
recipes.equipment: knife · dry pan (or a toaster) — no heat needed beyond toasting
recipes.eats: seeded wholemeal bread, tinned sardines, avocado, pumpkin seeds

summary.steps: soak sliced onion in vinegar + salt → toast bread, rub with cut garlic, drizzle oil → mash avocado on top with lemon, salt → fork over sardines → finish with onion, chilli, lemon, oil, pumpkin seeds, pepper

recipes.blurb: The fastest omega-3 hit in the set and the one you'd actually crave: ripe avocado smashed onto garlic-rubbed seeded toast, tinned sardines forked in with a big squeeze of lemon, chilli and oil over the top. The creamy avocado fat rounds off the strong fish and carries the lemon; the seeded bread gives bite and fibre. The only heat is the toaster.
method: Toss the sliced onion with the red wine vinegar and a pinch of salt in a small bowl; leave it to soften and turn sharp-sweet while you do everything else.
Toast the bread until deep golden — in a dry pan over medium heat (a couple of minutes a side) or in a toaster. Rub each hot slice with the cut face of the garlic and drizzle with a little olive oil.
Halve the avocado, scoop onto the toast, and mash it down with a fork. Squeeze over a little lemon and season with salt and pepper.
Fork the sardines over the avocado in big flakes, breaking them just enough to spread, and squeeze on more lemon.
Scatter over the pickled onion, chilli flakes and pumpkin seeds, finish with a thread of olive oil and a grind of pepper, and eat straight away while the toast is crisp.
levelUp: **Heat underneath (+ harissa or sriracha, not in kit):** a thin smear under the avocado adds a warm, smoky background that loves the oily fish.
**Briny pop (+ capers or chopped gherkins, not in kit):** a scatter of either cuts the richness and makes it taste more like a proper sardine tartine.
**Herb lift (+ fresh dill or parsley, not in kit):** a pinch torn over the top brightens everything and pairs naturally with sardines.
**Better bread (+ sourdough or rye, not in kit):** a sturdy slice toasts crisper and holds the smash without going soggy.
recipes.why: Effort leads, and hard — one board, a fork and the toaster, done in under ten minutes with nothing to watch or wash up. Nutrition rides along for free: bone-in sardines bring omega-3, B12, vitamin D and calcium, the avocado adds healthy fat and potassium, and the seeded bread plus pumpkin seeds pile on fibre. Every item is an ordinary supermarket staple, and the lemon-against-creamy-avocado-against-salty-fish balance makes it genuinely crave-able.

recipes.title: Sardine, Orange & Red-Onion Salad over Spinach
recipes.eats: tinned sardines, orange, spinach

summary.steps: macerate thinly sliced onion in vinegar + salt → segment the orange → dress spinach with oil, salt, pepper → lay orange and onion over, flake sardines on top, finish with oil, chilli and pepper

recipes.blurb: The Sicilian move: sweet orange against oily fish. The citrus cuts the richness of the sardines and brightens the whole plate, and its vitamin C helps your body pull iron from the spinach and fish. An elegant no-cook dish — knife and bowl only.
ingredients: 1 tin sardines (in oil or water), drained
¼ red onion, very thinly sliced
2 big handfuls spinach (fresh; tear if leaves are large)
Extra-virgin olive oil, fine sea salt, black pepper
method: In your serving bowl, toss the sliced onion with the vinegar and a pinch of salt. Leave it to soften and lose its raw bite while you do the rest.

Segment the orange: slice off the top and bottom, stand it up and cut the peel and white pith away in strips, then cut between the membranes to free the segments (or just slice into thin rounds). Save any juice.
Pile the spinach onto a plate or wide bowl and dress with a good glug of olive oil, a little of the saved orange juice, salt and black pepper. Toss to coat and lightly wilt.
Lay the orange and the macerated onion over the spinach, then flake the sardines on top. Finish with another drizzle of oil, the chilli flakes and plenty of black pepper.
levelUp: **Sicilian classic (+ shaved fennel, not in kit):** shave a little raw fennel through for the traditional aniseed crunch that pairs with orange.
**Brine & mint (+ olives and fresh mint, not in kit):** scatter black olives and torn mint for a salty, fragrant lift.
**Crunch on top (+ toasted almonds or pumpkin seeds, in kit):** toast a handful in a dry pan and scatter over for texture and extra healthy fat.
**Jewelled finish (+ pomegranate seeds, not in kit):** a handful adds pops of sweet-tart juice and colour.
recipes.why: Dominant criterion is **nutrition** — tinned sardines stack omega-3, complete protein, calcium, vitamin D and B12; spinach brings iron and folate; and the orange's vitamin C measurably boosts how much of that iron you absorb, all carried in olive oil (nutrition 🟢). It's genuinely good to eat, the sweet-citrus-against-oily-fish hook doing real work (taste 🟢), and there's no cooking at all — a knife, a bowl and one continuous session, from all-supermarket staples (effort 🟢, availability 🟢).

summary.steps: temper onion, garlic, cumin & chilli in oil → stir in oats, water & peas, simmer to creamy → fry the egg in the same pan → plate the oats, top with egg, lemon & a pinch more chilli

method: Heat the oil in a pan over medium. Soften the onion 3–4 min, then add the garlic, cumin and chilli flakes and fry ~1 min until fragrant.

Stir in the oats to toast for 30 sec, pour in the water and tip in the frozen peas. Simmer, stirring now and then, 4–5 min until creamy and the oats are tender. Season with salt and pepper, then scrape onto a plate.
Wipe the pan quickly if it's wet and add a touch more oil if needed, then crack the egg(s) straight into the hot pan and fry to your liking — cover for a soft-set top. Slide it onto the oats.
Squeeze over lemon, add a final pinch of chilli, and eat hot.

recipes.title: Smoky Cumin Chickpea Chilli
recipes.eats: canned chickpeas, bell pepper, tinned chopped tomato

summary.steps: hard-brown the onion in oil → soften pepper, then bloom garlic, cumin, chilli → add tomato + chickpeas, mash a few, simmer thick → sharpen with red wine vinegar, salt, pepper

recipes.blurb: A thick one-pot chilli where bloomed cumin and a hard-browned onion stand in for a whole spice rack — and it only gets better reheated the next day.
method: Warm a good glug of olive oil in the pot over medium-high. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring now and then, until deep golden-brown at the edges — 8–10 min. This browning is most of the flavour, so let it go further than feels comfortable.
Stir in the bell pepper and cook 3–4 min until it slumps.
Drop the heat, add the garlic, cumin and chilli flakes, and toss ~1 min until fragrant and the cumin smells toasty.

Pour in the tomatoes and chickpeas, season with salt and pepper, and bring to a simmer. Mash a handful of the chickpeas against the side of the pot to thicken. Simmer, stirring occasionally, 12–15 min, until thick enough to hold a spoon-trail.
Off the heat, stir in the red wine vinegar and taste for salt and heat. Serve, or cool and reheat tomorrow when it's even better.
levelUp: **Deeper smoke (+ smoked paprika, not in kit):** a teaspoon with the cumin pushes it from chilli-flake heat toward proper barbecue depth.
**Bulk it out (+ kidney or black beans, not in kit):** tip in a drained can alongside the chickpeas for a heartier, two-bean chilli that stretches to more servings.

**Make it a plate (+ rice, corn tortillas, avocado, coriander or lime, not in kit):** spoon over rice or roll into tortillas, then finish with sliced avocado, coriander and a squeeze of lime; (+ grated cheddar or feta, not in kit) melts in for a richer bowl.
recipes.why: Taste leads — a hard-browned onion plus bloomed cumin builds a smoky, savoury base that tastes slow-cooked from two spices, and reheating only deepens it. It's also genuinely nutrient-dense (chickpea protein and fibre, vit-C-rich pepper and tomato, olive oil for healthy fat), every item is an ordinary shelf staple, and it's one pot in one continuous session.

recipes.title: Smoky Hummus Toast with Frizzled Egg & Chilli Oil
recipes.eats: wholemeal / seeded sliced bread, hummus, eggs

summary.steps: toast the bread → spread thick with hummus → frizzle an egg in hot oil till the edges are lacy and crisp, slide it onto the hummus → bloom paprika & chilli in the same hot oil and pour over → finish with lemon, salt, pepper

recipes.blurb: A café plate in five minutes: thick hummus on hot toast, a crispy-edged frizzled egg on top, and a quick paprika-chilli oil poured over so it pools into the hummus. Hummus does the work of cooked chickpeas with none of the cooking, so it's the fastest hot, complete-protein dish in the set.
ingredients: Extra-virgin olive oil (a generous 2–3 tbsp — the egg frizzles in it)
method: Toast the bread — in a toaster, or dry in the pan over medium heat until crisp on both sides. Spread each slice thickly with hummus and set on your plate.

Wipe the pan, add the olive oil and set over medium-high until it shimmers. Crack in the eggs and let them sit undisturbed so the edges blister, bubble and frizzle into crisp lace; tilt the pan and spoon hot oil over the whites until set but the yolks stay runny, 1–2 min. Lay an egg on each hummus toast.

Drop the heat to low. Into the oil left in the pan (top up with a splash if dry), stir the smoked paprika and chilli flakes and bloom for 15–20 sec — just until fragrant and the oil turns red; don't let the paprika scorch.
Spoon the warm chilli oil over the eggs and toast so it pools into the hummus. Squeeze over lemon, season with salt and black pepper, and eat straight away.
levelUp: **Nutty crunch (+ dukkah or za'atar, not in kit):** a spoon scattered over at the end adds toasty, seedy texture against the soft hummus and yolk.

recipes.title: Tarka Dal (Quick Turmeric Red Lentil Dal)
recipes.eats: red split lentils

summary.steps: soften onion in oil → add lentils, water, turmeric, cumin, coriander, ginger, bay; simmer until collapsed → season, whisk smooth, brighten with lemon → sizzle garlic, cumin, chilli in hot oil 60s and pour the crackling tarka over

recipes.blurb: The benchmark red-lentil dish and the one to learn first: lentils simmered soft with turmeric until they collapse, then finished with a tarka — garlic, cumin and chilli sizzled in hot oil and poured over so it crackles. That 60-second sizzle is the whole trick that makes cheap lentils crave-worthy, and it's the single most useful spice technique in the kit.
ingredients: 1½ tsp ground cumin (split: 1 tsp for the pot, ½ tsp for the tarka)
method: Rinse the lentils in a sieve or by swirling in the pot and pouring off the cloudy water two or three times.
Warm a glug of olive oil in the pot over medium heat and soften the onion with a pinch of salt, ~5 min, until translucent — you want it soft and sweet, not browned.

Add the lentils, 600ml water, turmeric, 1 tsp cumin, the coriander, ginger and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then drop to a low simmer for 20–25 min, stirring now and then and skimming off any foam, until the lentils slump into a loose porridge. Splash in more water if it tightens too much.

Season well with salt and black pepper, then whisk briskly to break the lentils smooth and loosen to a pourable-but-spoonable consistency. Squeeze in lemon to taste. Pull out the bay leaf and keep the dal warm on the lowest heat.

**The tarka:** in the small pan, heat 2 tbsp olive oil over medium-high until it shimmers. Add the sliced garlic and fry 30–45s until pale gold, then take the pan off the heat and tip in the remaining ½ tsp cumin and the chilli flakes — they'll crackle and bloom in the hot oil. Pour the whole sizzling lot, oil and all, over the dal. Stir half through and leave the rest pooled on top. Serve as is, or with bread or rice.
levelUp: **Richer tarka (+ butter or ghee, not in kit):** melt a knob into the hot oil before the garlic for a rounder, restaurant-style finish.
**Brighter, sharper dal (+ fresh ginger and green chilli, not in kit):** grate fresh ginger into the simmer and slice a green chilli into the tarka for a livelier heat than the ground spices give.
**Classic South Indian finish (+ black mustard seeds and curry leaves, not in kit):** start the tarka with mustard seeds until they pop, then add a few curry leaves with the garlic.
**Veg-loaded dal (spinach or tomato, in kit):** wilt a couple of handfuls of spinach into the finished dal, or stir a chopped fresh tomato in with the lentils for a fuller, brothier bowl.
recipes.why: Nutrition leads — red lentils pack protein and fibre per serving for almost nothing, with turmeric and olive oil along for the ride, and it's naturally vegan and reheats brilliantly. Taste is what makes it a keeper: the poured-over tarka turns a plain pot of lentils crave-worthy. Every item is an ordinary shelf staple, and it's essentially one pot in one continuous session.

A small handful (~20g) almonds, roughly chopped
Splash of water; pinch of fine sea salt (optional)
method: Set a dry pan over medium heat. Tip in the oats, chopped almonds and pumpkin seeds and toast, tossing often, 3–4 min until the oats smell nutty and the seeds start to pop. Scrape onto a plate.

Return the pan to the heat, add the frozen berries with a splash of water and a tiny pinch of salt. Simmer, stirring and gently crushing, ~3 min until they collapse into a loose, glossy jam. Take off the heat.
Meanwhile, mash the banana into the Greek yoghurt in your bowl with a fork until smooth — it sweetens and loosens the yoghurt without any sugar.

Spoon the warm berry compote over the yoghurt so it ripples through, scatter the toasted oats, almonds and seeds over the top, and finish with a dusting of cinnamon. Eat while the berries are still warm against the cold yoghurt.
levelUp: **Sweeten if needed (+ honey or maple, not in kit):** a thread over the top or stirred into the compote, for days your banana isn't quite ripe enough to carry it.
**More body & omega-3 (+ ground flaxseed or chia, not in kit):** a spoon stirred through the yoghurt thickens it to an almost mousse-like set and adds omega-3.
**Halva note (+ tahini, not in kit):** a swirl through the yoghurt brings a nutty, savoury-sweet edge that plays off the berries.
**Fresh & crunchy top (+ fresh berries or granola, not in kit):** scatter over at the end for a pop of fresh fruit or extra crunch alongside the toasted oats.
recipes.why: Nutrition leads — Greek yoghurt and almonds bring protein and healthy fat, oats and berries the fibre and antioxidants, pumpkin seeds magnesium and zinc, all in one bowl with no added sugar. Effort keeps right up: one dry pan, one continuous session, ~10 minutes start to spoon, and no soaking ahead. Every item is an ordinary supermarket staple, and taste is the quiet win — warm jammy compote melting into cold creamy banana-sweet yoghurt under a toasty crunch tastes like a treat, not a health chore.

veganVariant.note: Only the Greek yoghurt needs to change — thick coconut or soy yoghurt gives the same creamy, protein-carrying base.
swaps: Replace the 150–200g Greek yoghurt with the same quantity of thick coconut or soy yoghurt
If using the optional sweetener from 'Level it up', use maple syrup rather than honey

frozen-mixed-berries.display: A large handful (~75g) frozen mixed berries

almonds.display: A small handful (~20g) almonds, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: Spinach
ingredients.why: One of the most nutrient-dense greens, and it cooks instantly in any pan.
ingredients.nutritionNote: vit K, vit A, folate, magnesium
ingredients.summary: The most effort-free nutrient hit in the kitchen — zero prep, wilts into any hot dish in 30–60 seconds, and delivers vitamin K, vitamin A, folate and magnesium in every handful.
tips: Add it last and pull the pan off the heat the moment it collapses — 30–60 seconds is enough, and another minute makes it grey and watery.
Eat it alongside a vitamin C source in the same meal — lemon, tomato or bell pepper — because spinach iron is oxalate-bound and vitamin C substantially improves how much you absorb.
Use fresh leaves raw as a salad base; dress with oil and acid and leave for two minutes — the acid softens the leaves slightly without cooking them.
With frozen, defrost slightly and squeeze out the water before it goes in the pan, or it will steam everything instead of wilting cleanly.
swaps: Keep a bag of frozen spinach in the freezer — it lasts 3 months, is already blanched, and goes straight into hot dishes after a quick squeeze.
Kale swaps in for any cooked dish; strip the tough stems and give it 4–5 extra minutes, expecting a firmer bite.
Rocket or watercress work in place of raw spinach in salads, with more peppery character.
ingredients.storage: Fresh spinach keeps 2–3 days in the fridge, unwashed and loosely bagged; frozen keeps for 3 months and is the more practical choice for most kitchens.

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.why: Eat raw or collapse into a quick sauce; tinned backup year-round.
ingredients.summary: Fresh or tinned, the tomato delivers acid, umami, and body in a single ingredient — the backbone of quick sauces, braises, and salads with almost no effort.
tips: Never refrigerate ripe tomatoes — cold kills their flavour and turns the flesh mealy.
Salt cut tomatoes and leave them 10 minutes before using in salads; you get concentrated flavour and the right texture.
Outside peak season (roughly July–September in the UK), reach for tinned plum tomatoes over fresh — they are riper, cheaper, and far more consistent.
Crush whole tinned tomatoes by hand straight into the pan so you control the texture and avoid watery lumps.
swaps: Tinned whole plum tomatoes are the year-round default — better than pale, out-of-season fresh ones for anything cooked.
Passata works wherever you want a smooth sauce without bothering to blend.
A spoonful of tomato purée stirred in at the start deepens colour and umami in any slow-cooked dish.
ingredients.storage: Store ripe tomatoes at room temperature stem-side down, away from direct sun — they keep 3–5 days; refrigerate only once cut and use within 2 days.

ingredients.name: Bell pepper
ingredients.why: Very high vit C (red especially), sweet; great raw or quick-fried.
ingredients.summary: A sweet, crunchy vegetable packed with vitamin C that adds colour, body, and natural sweetness to everyday cooking with almost no effort.
tips: Cut out the white pith — it's bitter and worth the extra ten seconds.

Roast whole directly over a gas flame or under a hot grill until blackened all over, then steam in a covered bowl for 10 minutes and peel — the flesh underneath is silky and sweet, nothing like the raw version.
Add raw strips late in a stir-fry if you want crunch; add early if you want them to melt into the sauce.
Red, yellow, and orange are ripe (sweeter); green are unripe (sharper, slightly bitter) — choose accordingly rather than by habit.
swaps: Jarred roasted red peppers are a straight, no-cook swap for cooked bell pepper in sauces, dips, and pasta.
Courgette or sugar snap peas give similar crunch in a stir-fry or raw salad when you're out.
A mild poblano or Anaheim chilli works if you want the same sweetness with a gentle background heat.
ingredients.storage: Store whole peppers in the fridge crisper drawer — they last up to 10 days; once cut, wrap tightly and use within 3 days.

ingredients.name: Broccoli
ingredients.why: Top-tier brassica nutrition; stir-fry small florets, just needs cutting.
ingredients.nutritionNote: vit C, vit K, folate, sulforaphane
ingredients.summary: A fast-cooking, nutrient-dense brassica that works roasted, steamed, or stir-fried and earns its keep in any low-effort kitchen by turning a bare fridge into a proper meal.
tips: Cut the stalk into coins and cook them alongside the florets — they're sweeter than the top and go to waste for no reason.
Dry the florets completely before roasting, then use high heat (220 °C) so they char at the edges rather than steam into mush.
Don't overcook it: two to three minutes in well-salted boiling water keeps it bright green and with some bite.
Add a splash of acid — lemon juice or vinegar — just before serving to lift the whole dish.
swaps: Frozen broccoli is just as good in cooked dishes — tip it straight from frozen into a hot pan or boiling water.
Tenderstem (broccolini) is a direct swap and needs no chopping; roast or griddle whole.
Cauliflower works in place of broccoli in any recipe where it will be cooked through.
ingredients.storage: Store unwashed in a loose bag in the fridge crisper drawer and use within five days before the florets yellow and the smell sharpens.

ingredients.name: Cabbage
ingredients.why: Cheap, keeps for weeks, shreds and stir-fries fast.
ingredients.summary: A tough, cheap brassica that keeps for weeks and earns its place by being equally good raw in a slaw, quickly charred in a hot pan, or braised low and slow into something sweet and tender.
tips: Salt shredded cabbage and leave it 10 minutes before dressing — it wilts to silk and stops the slaw turning watery.
Get the pan searingly hot before adding cabbage wedges cut-side down — dry heat caramelises the face and turns something bland into something genuinely sweet and complex.
Pull it off the heat while it still has bite — overcooking releases sulphur compounds and turns it grey and rank.
Add vinegar or lemon juice at the end of cooking to brighten both the colour and the flavour.
swaps: Savoy is softer and more yielding — use it when you want the cabbage to melt into a braise rather than hold its shape.
Hispi (sweetheart) cabbage halves and chars beautifully in less time than a round head, and has a more delicate flavour.
Pak choi substitutes well in any stir-fry or quick braise where you'd otherwise reach for cabbage.
ingredients.storage: Keep the whole head loosely wrapped in the fridge for up to 3 weeks; once cut, press cling film directly against the exposed face and use within a week.

ingredients.name: Carrot
